patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — commercetools and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose commercetools only if your buying job matches “Composable enterprise commerce API — quote-only packages + 60-day free trial; contact sale” rather than OpenCart's shape. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than commercetools's shape. Workflow advantage: commercetools leans wholesale-b2b; OpenCart leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — commercetools and OpenCart share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: commercetools is Composable enterprise commerce API — quote-only packages + 60-day free trial; contact sales. Shopify keeps the SaaS award.; OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee.
- Company-size focus: commercetools (mid-market, enterprise) vs OpenCart (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: commercetools-leaning wholesale-b2b vs OpenCart-leaning —.
- Researched limits: commercetools — No published monthly list price — hard to compare without a sales worksheet; OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0.

Limitations — commercetools: No published monthly list price — hard to compare without a sales worksheet; Requires front-end / MACH assembly — not a weekend theme launch; OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting.

Poor-fit cases: commercetools is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No published monthly list price — hard to compare without a sales worksheet · OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Avoid commercetools if you actually need OpenCart's motion (GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
